scope: Three existing technical findings reviewed for explicitly attributed, isolated AI explanations only; this cases/source_units view is not a replacement source translation, role approval or closed production audit.

cases.finding: Successful calloc returns byte-zeroed storage. Avoiding redundant physical writes is an implementation optimization, not permission to expose uninitialized storage. A zeroing requirement may motivate calloc instead of malloc followed by memset, but performance is not universally better and byte zeroing is not C++ object construction.
preserved_constraints: do not substitute for C++ construction

cases.finding: jemalloc5.2.1 nallocx computes a size without allocating, sallocx queries a live allocation, and xallocx attempts an in-place resize whose returned size must be checked. sdallocx returns void, contrary to the source slide's size_t. Its supplied size ranges from the original request through a compatible nallocx/sallocx size; a type's sizeof alone is insufficient authority for that allocation.
preserved_constraints: original-request lower bound and compatible-size upper bound
cases.reading_recipe_authority: nallocx versus N alloc X, and sdallocx versus S D alloc X, are whole-sentence candidate readings, not official pronunciations or approved phoneme instructions. Exact identifiers remain in display.

cases.finding: jemalloc5.2.1 allocated and active are current byte-valued application-allocation and active-page measures, not cumulative requests or interchangeable page counts. For active greater than zero,1 - allocated/active is an approximate indicator, not a complete diagnosis. resident includes metadata and other allocator pages and the manual explicitly calls it a maximum rather than precise measurement; it is not exact whole-process RSS. The DHAT average-access issue remains outside these two statistics candidates' claimed scope.
preserved_constraints: active must be nonzero for ratio
resident includes metadata and is an upper-bound estimate
historical5.2.1 reference, not a guarantee for all installed versions
